All 31 families run exhaustively (every released question, 10,059 in total) by refs/choice_pass_geo_run.py with judges in refs/choice_pass_geo_a.py (elementary/vocabulary/figure families), choice_pass_geo_b.py (circle theorems, congruence/similarity, Ceva/Menelaus, triangle centres, proof reasons) and choice_pass_geo_c.py (coordinate families). Each judge decides per option whether it is correct from statement/figure only; the stored letter is used solely for the final comparison. Requirement per question: exactly one correct option and it is the keyed letter. Duplicate option texts: none. Prompts that a judge could not parse are Unsupported (none remain).

Key-shift mutation: a copy of the data with every key moved to the next option was run through the same judges (/tmp/certout/choice-pass-geo-mut/fam): 100% of the decidable questions were flagged mismatch in all 31 families (the 142 Ambiguous questions stay Ambiguous), so no judge is vacuous.

Word forms: the word prompt answer equals the typed answer in all questions (wordBad = 0). I read a sample of word prompts (first templates of 17 families): all restate the typed question faithfully (same numbers/figure); wording beyond that is not verified.

aiconvex: the degenerate group (coordinates A,B,C collinear, params [1,2,k]; and the angle version with an interior angle of 180 degrees, params [0,2,k]) is returned Ambiguous and registered separately (strict definition: triangle, so not a quadrilateral; weak definition: degenerate convex quadrilateral). All other 159 questions: angle sum 360 with all angles < 180 = convex, exactly one > 180 = concave, sum != 360 = impossible; coordinates by edge-turn signs and crossing tests.

amsimc group [4,*,*] (72 questions): two proportional sides + equal non-included angle with the OPPOSITE side longer than the adjacent side determines the triangle uniquely, so ABC and PQR are in fact similar; the keyed 'Not shown to be similar' is true only as 'not by AA/SAS/SSS'. Returned Ambiguous and registered (medium). The other 264 are verified with 'not shown' read as 'AA/SSS/SAS do not apply'.

amcrit: rules are applied to the facts literally listed (SSS; SAS = two sides + included angle; ASA = two angles + included side; AAS = two angles + non-included side; RHS = right angle at the vertex opposite the given side + that side + one more side). 'None of these' is correct iff the facts leave more than one triangle (explicit SSA root count by the law of cosines; every released 'None of these' item is a two-solution SSA case (no Defect arose)). ASA and AAS are interchangeable once the third angle is deduced; the 100 items of groups [2,*,*]/[3,*,*] offer both, so a low-severity ambiguity is registered although the runner counts them verified under the literal reading.

Vocabulary / figure-matching families were checked against standard textbook definitions: aecpart/alcvoc (centre, radius, chord = both ends on the circle, diameter = chord through the centre, arc, sector = region between two radii and an arc, segment = region between a chord and an arc, circumference, a circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry = every line through the centre, maps onto itself under every rotation about the centre, a reflection in a line through the centre preserves the distance from the centre so the image lies on the same circle); a diameter is also a chord, so a diameter item that also offered 'a chord' would be multiply correct (never happens).

aearms: the vertex of angle ABC is the middle letter; its arms are the two rays from the vertex through the end letters (the 'line segment AC' and rays from other letters are wrong); angle size does not depend on arm length, clock-hand turn = 30 degrees per hour mark.

awctr: centroid/circumcentre/orthocentre/incentre computed exactly on a scalene 13-14-15 triangle (centroid from the plate's first-moment formula, circumcentre by equal distances, orthocentre by altitudes, incentre by equal signed distances to the sides); every stem property is tested for each of the four centres and exactly one must satisfy it. Right-angle items use the 3-4-5 triangle (orthocentre = right-angle vertex, circumcentre = midpoint of the hypotenuse). Line-classification items (altitude/median/angle bisector/perpendicular bisector) are judged on the scalene triangle, so only properties implied by the stem count (e.g. AD with BD = DC is a median, not 'the perpendicular bisector'). The four lines per centre (medians, altitudes, perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors) are tested by incidence.

altheo/amreason: the configuration is classified from the wording (centre vs circumference, same side of a chord, opposite vertices of a cyclic quadrilateral, diameter, perpendicular from the centre, equal chords; crossing lines, straight line, parallel lines with transversal, triangle sum, exterior angle) and the stated numeric step is checked (x2, equal, 90 and complement, 180-x, doubled half-chord, equal distances, sum of two). The two false statements ('same-segment angles add up to 180', 'opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are equal') are never correct. Standard statements: NCERT class 9 ch.10 and ch.6.

afcube: nets are folded physically by rolling a die over the squares (a net is valid iff the six cells receive six different die faces; two letters are opposite iff their die faces are opposite); afnet: solids are data (net faces, view from above, front view standing, end view lying) generated from standard definitions (prism = 2 n-gons + n rectangles, pyramid = 1 n-gon + n triangles); squares count as rectangles (a cube is a cuboid), so an item offering both would be flagged (never happens).

aemirror: certifier's own sans-serif glyph tables: left-right symmetric A H I M O T U V W X Y (standing mirror: word unchanged iff all letters are in this set and the word is a palindrome); up-down symmetric B C D E H I K O X (still-water reflection: order unchanged, every letter must be up-down symmetric). aertang: everyday corner sizes (notebook, postcard, blackboard, door, tile, matchbox, carrom board, wall-floor = 90; open book flat = 180; pizza slice of 8 = 45; honeycomb cell = 120; sharpened pencil, rangoli star tip, samosa corner are acute (assumed 30/36/60)); clock hands at h o'clock = smaller angle 30h; only angle = 90 is right.

afkind: inclusive definitions (square is a rectangle and a rhombus; rhombus is a kite and a parallelogram), trapezium = exactly one pair of parallel sides; the best name is the true name implying all other true names; angles of a parallelogram checked for consistency (co-interior angles add to 180). au3cl: an equilateral triangle would be Ambiguous (no equilateral option); none occurs. arcone: plane angle 0 degrees with the axis (parallel to the axis) is allowed: hyperbola (not through the vertex) / pair of lines (through the vertex). arxyconic: eigen-decomposition of the quadratic form plus the 3x3 determinant (degenerate/imaginary conics would be Ambiguous/Defect; none occur).

ambptc: converse of the basic proportionality theorem tested with D on AB and E on AC placed on perpendicular axes (parallel iff AE*DB = AD*EC); converse of the angle-bisector theorem tested by building the triangle from three sides (law of cosines) and comparing angles BAD and DAC exactly; 'cannot be decided' is never correct because lengths are given. ammen: Ceva (concurrency) and Menelaus (D beyond C, E and F interior) tested by coordinates in two different non-special triangles, results agree in every case.
